claims.text: A geometric deep-learning model such as an E(3)NN can use full 3D atomic structures and crystallographic symmetry to predict phonon density of states and derived thermal properties.
The proposed model will correctly identify high-entropy alloys with exceptionally low phonon thermal conductivity.
GeTe-based and PbSe-based chalcogenides are examples of multi-element high-entropy compounds relevant to the proposed application.
The model can calculate phonon density of states and related quantities such as Debye temperature and dominant phonon wavelength for HEAs.
GeTe-based and PbSe-based high-entropy compounds have applications at mid and high temperatures.
An accurate geometric representation of atomic arrangements and crystallographic symmetry captures structural information relevant to phonon scattering.
Preserving 3D translational, rotational, and inversion symmetries allows an E(3)NN to extract useful atomic-scale features efficiently.
Mass disorder and strain fluctuations drive phonon-scattering events in the targeted HEAs.
Strengthening phonon scattering can reduce thermal conductivity in high-entropy chalcogenide compounds.
More accurate phonon-density-of-states predictions will consequently produce more accurate lattice-thermal-conductivity predictions.
The model will improve lattice-thermal-conductivity predictive accuracy by at least 20–30% relative to discrete-point methods or virtual-crystal approximations.
Many existing materials-property studies predict only one or a few discrete output values.
Virtual-crystal approximations may fail to capture the interplay of multi-element disorder and symmetry in HEAs.
The approach is primarily applicable to crystalline HEAs with well-defined atomic positions.
Reliability will diminish for amorphous or poorly characterized materials and for compositions far outside the training domain.
Limited training-data volume is a challenge for predicting complex continuous material properties.
Defects and grain boundaries under experimental conditions may reduce accuracy because they may not be represented by the model.
Reduced dominant phonon wavelengths are characteristic of enhanced phonon scattering in the proposed HEAs.
A greater-than-25% discrepancy between predicted and measured lattice thermal conductivity for a statistically significant number of selected HEAs is designated as a falsifying outcome.
